(re @dannyryan: Least invasive is probably Two values * max-ed-size for compile time * el-max-ed-size instantoated per net El-max-ed-size has a validation on consensus to make sure the ed isnt overflown before passing to el) <sigpaul> Does the CL need to check it before sending it to the EL? excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<n0ble> @vdWijden the preparePayload with unknown parent case is specified in the Interop spec here: https://hackmd.io/@n0ble/merge-interop-spec#Engine-API1
I think that in production it should have a block tree inconsistency kind of error that could initiate a recovery assuming that a failure has happened that lead CL and EL to an inconsistent state. This is to be discussed (message ordering and constistency + recovery mechanics)
Any other execution errors (not related to the consistency issue) are not necessarily needed for CL but could be returned and logged to provide addition information about execution payload invalidity reason

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <n0ble> Forwarded from vdWijden: Both maybe? I've implemented the two errors that you specified in the merge spec, but there are a lot of other errors that can happen during execution that are currently underspecified. (e.g. preparePayload with unknown parent,...)

excerpts.content:
<vdWijden> I have a general questions regarding the API on the EL side. Previously I didn't check whether the parent block surpasses the TTD in ForkchoiceUpdated and in ConsensusValidated. In ExecutePayload I now check that the parent block surpasses the TDD iff the node is synced. 
I think those checks should be part of the spec imo. This does mean that the three methods fail if we don't have the parent available.
